plan.structureSummary: The rule takes the submitted ticket (a list of six distinct numbers) and uses a reduce operation to find its maximum and minimum values. runs.proposal: Only tickets matching at least two drawn numbers are eligible. Among eligible tickets, the ticket with the smallest difference between its highest and lowest number wins; all ties win and share the prize.

plan.structureSummary: The decision model first intersects the ticket list with the draw list and counts how many numbers match, keeping only tickets with a count of at least two. For each eligible ticket it computes the range (max minus min) of its numbers and selects the smallest range; all tickets tied for the smallest range win.

runs.proposal: Separe os números do jogo entre acertados e não acertados. O jogador ganha se algum número não acertado tiver o mesmo algarismo das unidades que algum número acertado.

plan.structureSummary: The rule first splits the draw list into the numbers that were guessed correctly (the intersection of ticket and draw) and the numbers that were not guessed (the draw list minus the ticket). It then maps each of those two lists to their unit digits using the digits operation. Finally it checks whether there exists at least one non‑matched number whose unit digit equals the unit digit of some matched number; if such a pair exists the player wins.

plan.structureSummary: The rule first filters the submitted tickets, keeping only those whose total sum is less than the sum of the drawn numbers. For each surviving ticket it extracts the unit digit of each of its six numbers, discards duplicates, and counts the distinct unit digits; this count becomes the ticket's score. The ranking selects the ticket(s) with the highest count, and any ties split the prize.

runs.proposal: The player wins only when exactly one of these three statements is true: at least three guessed numbers were drawn; the guessed numbers sum to more than the drawn numbers; the player's highest number was drawn.

plan.structureSummary: The tree first builds three boolean branches: (1) compute the intersection of the ticket and draw lists, reduce it by count, and compare the count to the constant 3; (2) reduce each list by sum and compare the ticket sum to the draw sum; (3) reduce the ticket list by max and test whether that max value is contained in the draw list. These three booleans are then combined with logical operators so that exactly one of them is true (exclusive‑or).
